subject: Zero-trust preflight & storage allocation for on-prem cluster — SilverLine

From: Samir Shah <samir@silverlinehealth.com>

Date: 2027-04-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PV/Node sizing questions ahead of on-prem deployment

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. To prep our internal ops team I wanted to capture a few specific asks and constraints so your delivery team can validate:

- Zero-trust requirement: everything must authenticate mutually (mTLS) and be limited by L4 policies between namespaces; control-plane API must not be reachable from general tenant networks.
- Storage: primary persistent store for model KV cache and uploads needs encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS preferred) and snapshot capability. Expected working set: ~6 TB hot (KV + model checkpoints) with heavy small-block reads (~10–20k IOPS spike).
- Node pools: we plan to run mixed workloads — GPU inference (A100 equivalence), CPU batch, and a small control-plane footprint. We need suggested node profiles and an idea of local NVMe vs network volumes tradeoffs.
- Networking: we have L2 fiber in the rack, BGP to leafs, and can expose a private peering to Redwood if needed. We also require audit logs and flow logs to be delivered to our SIEM.

I've attached our site inventory spreadsheet (site-ops-inventory.xlsx) and the SOC2 Q&A we did internally — can you confirm what of that you need from us?

High-level timeline: procurement wants a signed SOW by mid-May to meet our rollout windows. Procurement (procurement@silverlinehealth.com) is copied.

Can you send a short preflight checklist + recommended node/storage configurations so we can get a technical review scheduled?

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Infrastructure
SilverLine Health

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the inventory. Attaching a concise preflight and a node-profile workbook to get the technical review started. High level answers and next steps below.

Summary answers (short):
- Zero-trust: we recommend enforcing mTLS for all service-to-service traffic via a lightweight mesh (istio/consul/envoy) or using a strict CNI + network policy posture (Calico with egress rules). Control-plane endpoints should sit on a dedicated management VLAN and be accessible only via the Redwood VPN peering or a jump host with bastion + MFA.
- Storage & encryption: prefer customer-managed KMS for disk encryption. For hot KV cache we recommend NVMe-backed local volumes for lowest latency, surfaced via a replicated blockstore (Ceph/Rook or external SAN) depending on your ops preference. Snapshotting via built-in scheduler (Velero) to an object store.
- Node profiles (recommended starter set):
  * control-plane: 3x r6.large-equivalent dedicated masters (no GPU), hardened, RHEL 8, separate etcd nodes if you want dedicated etcd hosts.
  * inference-GPU pool: 4–8x GPU nodes (96GB RAM, NVMe scratch, 1–2x A100-equivalent GPUs); use local NVMe for KV cache, but mount as encrypted volumes.
  * cpu-batch pool: 6–12x CPU nodes (compact vCPU-dense), network-attached storage OK for model artifacts and long-term checkpoints.
  * infra/cache pool: 2–3 nodes with high IOPS NVMe (20k IOPS target sustained), 2–4 TB each for sharded KV volumes.

Networking notes:
- We'll use private peering (BGP) from your leafs to Redwood egress. BFD not required initially but recommended for faster failover.
- Egress routing: policy-based egress via NAT GW or dedicated egress nodes; we can also push per-tenant IP allowlists.
- Logging: flow logs (sFlow/IPFIX) can be exported to your SIEM; audit logs from kube-apiserver and our agent will be forwarded to your S3-compatible endpoint.

Preflight asks (what we need from you):
- Switch port map and vlan plan for management and tenant networks.
- Public/private IP blocks to reserve for control-plane and services.
- KMS endpoint details and HSM requirements if any.
- Expected retention window for PV snapshots and backup frequency.

I've looped in Vivek (serving runtime lead) and Irene (customer on-prem eng) to validate storage IO targets and to propose a short technical validation call. Proposed time: Friday 2027-04-30 10:00 PT. If that works, we can send a calendar invite and a short preflight checklist to your ops team.

Attachments: redwood-node-profile.xlsx, k8s-preflight-checklist.md, silverline-soc2-q-a.pdf

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi / team — quick technical notes after reviewing the inventory and Rishi's recommendations. Quoting Samir's storage/IO callouts below.

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 12:05 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Storage & encryption: prefer customer-managed KMS for disk encryption. For hot KV cache we recommend NVMe-backed local volumes for lowest latency, surfaced via a replicated blockstore (Ceph/Rook or external SAN) depending on your ops preference.

Tech details / proposed changes:
- Control plane: prefer 3 dedicated master nodes and 3 dedicated etcd replicas. If hardware constrained, colocate etcd but keep etcd on journaled, encrypted, low-latency NVMe.
- Storage classes: create two SCs:
  * fast-replicated-nvme (Heavily provisioned, RWX not required) — use for KV cache and small-block heavy workloads. Provision: 2–4 vdisks per PV striped, target 15–25k IOPS per PV.
  * bulk-block-snap (replicated SAN/object backend) — for model artifacts and checkpoints; snapshots enabled daily.
- Encryption: integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud-KMS connector. If HSM required, coordinate certs ahead of the preflight. Use LUKS/dm-crypt for local nodes plus kernel keyring integration for automatic mount.
- IOPS sizing: for the 6 TB hot working set, plan for 1.5x headroom — target 30 TB aggregated capacity across NVMe nodes to reduce hot-sharding.
- Kubernetes flags: kubelet --rotate-certificates enabled, kube-apiserver audit-policy strict with passthrough to SIEM, kube-controller-manager snapshot-controller enabled.

Operational runbook items to include in preflight checklist:
- Validate time sync (NTP/Chrony) across all hosts — critical for cert rotation.
- Validate CPU pinning on GPU nodes and isolate CPU pools for system daemons.
- Stress test PVs with fio using small random reads (4k) at target IOPS for 30 minutes.
- Confirm backup destination and restore drill before cutover.

I've attached an editable preflight checklist with the items we'll verify during the call. I'll own the storage/I/O validation and can join the May onboarding window.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
